tagline.text: A public market opened in 1912 in downtown Iloilo, reborn as three floors

location.label: Location
location.text: Corner of Iznart and Rizal Streets, City Proper, Iloilo City

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,000 (market browsing plus a light meal or snacks, per person, estimate)

children.text: This is the main public market of downtown Iloilo, opened on January 15, 1912. It reopened in late 2025 as a three-level building, and you can see it together with the Calle Real heritage street on foot.
Iloilo Central Market is a public market in City Proper, the heart of Iloilo City. Locals simply call it Central Market, and its old name is Tienda Mayor. Records say it opened on
January 15, 1912

, and it is described as one of the oldest public markets in the Philippines. It occupies the corner where Iznart Street meets Rizal Street. It sits at one end of the Calle Real heritage zone, so it works well as the start or the end of a walk past Spanish- and American-era buildings.
The building's history comes in layers. After the market opened, an Art Deco façade was added in
, and the first major renovation took place in
under Acting Mayor Rosa Caram. In
August 2022
, SM Prime Holdings was awarded a 25-year lease through a public-private partnership (PPP), which started the redevelopment. Reports put the project cost at about ₱3 billion.
The redevelopment also became a public controversy. In early

the Art Deco façade was demolished on structural-safety grounds, which drew criticism for damaging a heritage structure and even administrative complaints against the mayor. The city government and the developer pledged to reproduce the original design faithfully, and local media reported that the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) approved the city's revised plans. Reports differ on whether the demolition happened between February and April, so it is safest not to cite an exact month.
According to reports, the market wing opened on
October 30, 2025
, and the mall wing, SM Iloilo Central Market, opened on
November 28, 2025

. Some reports call it a soft opening, so check the opening status of individual shops before you visit. The city government continues to run the market wing, and the mayor said stall allocations and rental rates would stay at their existing levels. The one-story building became a three-level building, and vendor capacity grew to about 850, although reports differ slightly on the exact figure. For a traveler, the appeal is less a list of sights than a close look at how Ilonggos actually shop. Piles of fish and meat, dried goods, tropical fruit and vegetables, a meal at a market eatery, and then the old buildings of Calle Real and a riverside stroll can easily fill half a day. Because the redevelopment is so recent, the floor layout and opening hours may still change, so adjust to what you find on the spot. The Iloilo Terminal Market was reopened under the same project, and both markets were redeveloped by SM Prime with the city running operations.

blocks.title: A public market that began in 1912

children.text: The market formally opened on
January 15, 1912

. It is among the older public markets in the Philippines and has fed Iloilo residents for generations. Simply seeing a market site that is more than 100 years old in the middle of the city is worthwhile.
The market gained an Art Deco façade in
, and it was the market's face for a long time. After the demolition in
, an October 2025 report said it had been rebuilt. Judge for yourself how closely it matches the original.

blocks.title: A new market on three floors

children.text: Reports say the ground floor holds fresh-food stalls such as fish, meat, poultry and frozen goods. The second floor has dried goods, groceries, variety items, coconut grinders and produce, and the third floor has a food hall, eateries, service shops and offices. Each floor has its own character, so it is nice to browse from top to bottom.

According to the developer, there are zones and shared dining areas featuring Iloilo favorites such as batchoy, pancit molo and fresh seafood. Iloilo is famous for La Paz batchoy, so a meal at the market food corner doubles as a taste of local culture.

The developer says vendor capacity rose to about 850 and the mall wing has 61 long-term leasable spaces. The market wing is run by the city and the mall wing by SM, a two-part structure. Many market stalls have no price tags, so ask the price first.
According to Wikipedia and SunStar (April 2026), the city government's Market Day program lets transient vendors operate under a Lunesan schedule from
on Monday to
on Tuesday. Actual operation and hours after the reopening may change, so check on the spot.

blocks.title: The end of the Calle Real walk

children.text: The Calle Real heritage zone runs along Iznart Street to this market. Buildings in the zone from the 1920s include the Javellana Building (1922), the Villanueva Building (1927) and the Regent Theater (around 1928). We recommend starting at the market and walking past these buildings.

blocks.title: Large floor area and rooftop parking

children.text: According to the developer, SM Iloilo Central Market has more than

of floor area. One report also mentions rooftop parking for about 300 vehicles, but that description was part of a standard layout shared with the Terminal Market, so I could not confirm that it applies here. If you are driving, check on the spot.

items.title: Half-day market and street walk
items.subtitle: From the market to Calle Real

children.text: Arrive at the Central Market early. The morning is when the market is liveliest, and starting with the ground-floor fresh-food stalls gives you the best feel for the place.
Go up to the second floor and look around the dried goods, groceries and tropical fruit. Ask prices and compare before buying dried fish or snacks as souvenirs.
Have an early lunch or a snack at the third-floor food hall and eateries. If you see local dishes such as batchoy or pancit molo, try them.
Leave the market and walk along Iznart Street toward Calle Real, looking at the heritage buildings.
Rest at a nearby restaurant or café to escape the heat. In the afternoon, you could head to the Iloilo riverside promenade.

Opening times differ by shop and may change because the redevelopment is so recent. The market wing tends to open early and the mall wing often follows mall hours, but no confirmed hours were found. Check on the spot. The market wing is run by the city and the mall wing by SM, so even within one building the hours may differ.

items.title: Full-day downtown Iloilo
items.subtitle: From the market to the river

children.text: Browse the Central Market and have breakfast there.
Walk the Calle Real heritage street and photograph the building façades.
Take a taxi or tricycle to nearby sights such as Molo Church or Jaro Cathedral.
Take an evening walk along the Iloilo River Esplanade.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Iloilo International Airport (ILO), and flight time is about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change by season, so check when you book.
Iloilo International Airport is in Cabatuan, away from the city, so you reach downtown by airport van or taxi. Fares and travel times vary with traffic, so check on the spot.
I could not confirm the exact fare from the airport to the market.
Within City Proper, get around by taxi, ride-hailing app or jeepney.
The market is connected to the Calle Real heritage street, so you can often walk from nearby hotels. Check the exact distance on a map app.
The market is indoors, so weather matters little, but the dry season is more comfortable for walking around Iloilo. In general,
November–May
is relatively less humid and good for walking.

Early morning is the best time of day, because fresh food is most varied in the morning and midday is hot. In January the city's signature festival, Dinagyang, fills the whole city with crowds, so book your lodging early then.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Good walking season. Crowded during the Dinagyang Festival in January
Move around mostly in the early morning or evening
Indoor market browsing is fine. Bring an umbrella

items.label: Market entry
items.note: No entrance fee was found for this public market

items.label: Light meal at the market
items.note: Varies by shop. Ask first where there are no price tags

items.label: One meal at the food hall
Dried fish and snack souvenirs
items.note: Estimate, depends on weight and type

items.label: Tricycle or taxi (short trip in town)
items.note: Per city ordinance ₱15 for the first 2 km plus ₱1 per extra km (2022 report, same in a 2026 guide), about ₱50 minimum if riding alone. A fare increase is reportedly on hold. Agree on the fare before riding

items.label: Airport to downtown
items.note: Shared van (UV Express) fare is from SM City Iloilo and leaves only when full. Taxi is by meter. Grab is about ₱450~500 for a 4-seater (2025~2026 guides)

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

If you stay in City Proper, the downtown core, you can easily walk between the market and Calle Real. Areas near the riverside esplanade or SM City Iloilo are convenient to reach but are some distance from the market and may need transport. Check reviews and locations on booking sites before choosing a hotel.

Food is a big part of the market's appeal. Iloilo is known for batchoy, pancit molo and seafood, and according to the developer the market now has zones for this kind of local food. Hygiene and prices vary by shop, so choosing a busy stall with fast turnover is a sensible rule.

Along Iznart Street toward Calle Real, old buildings line the road, and Wikipedia mentions historic stores such as Hoskyn's department store, established in 1877. A coffee or snack there after the market shows you both old and new Iloilo at once. Check whether individual businesses are open when you visit.
Go early in the morning, when fresh food is at its best and it is less hot.
Many shops have no price tags, so ask the price before buying and compare two or three stalls.
Carry small bills for the market. Some shops reportedly accept QR payments, but it varies by shop.
Floors may be wet, so wear non-slip shoes.
After the market, walk the Calle Real heritage street along Iznart Street.
Because of the recent redevelopment, floor layouts and opening times may change. Check the latest information on Google Maps.
For souvenirs such as dried fish, check the packaging and airline carry-on rules before buying.
The market wing and the mall wing are run separately, so there may be two entrances. Check which side you are entering.
The market is crowded and pickpockets are a risk. Carry your bag in front and keep valuables out of sight.
Watch your phone and wallet in crowded times.
Fresh-food stalls can be smelly and humid, so if that bothers you, stick to the third-floor food hall.
This market was recently redeveloped, and its operations and hours may change, so check the latest announcements.
The area around the market is quiet at night, so do not travel alone late.
Choose street food only after looking at how clean the stall is.
The city the market belongs to, where you can visit other sights and restaurants downtown.
A riverside promenade close to downtown, good for an evening walk.
A historic cathedral reachable from downtown by taxi or jeepney. Travel time depends on traffic.
A well-known church on the outskirts of Iloilo, reached from downtown by car.
